note: Definitions paraphrase the SWM Rules, 2026 summary (PIB). Item guidance is a SAMPLE campus guide: edit or replace it with your own campus rules.

chunks.title: Wet waste (definition)
chunks.why: Wet waste is biodegradable kitchen and garden waste such as food scraps, fruit and vegetable peels, meat and flowers.
chunks.dispose: Put it in the wet waste bin so it can be composted or processed through bio-methanation.
chunks.source: SWM Rules, 2026 (MoEFCC)

chunks.title: Dry waste (definition)
chunks.why: Dry waste covers recyclable materials such as plastic, paper, metal, glass, wood and rubber.
chunks.dispose: Keep it clean and dry in the dry waste bin. It goes to a Material Recovery Facility for sorting and recycling.
chunks.source: SWM Rules, 2026 (MoEFCC)

chunks.title: Sanitary waste (definition)
chunks.why: Sanitary waste is used personal-hygiene items such as diapers, sanitary pads, tampons and condoms.
chunks.dispose: Wrap it securely and store it separately from other waste.
chunks.source: SWM Rules, 2026 (MoEFCC)

chunks.title: Special care waste (definition)
chunks.why: Special care waste is household hazardous waste such as paint cans, bulbs, mercury thermometers, batteries and expired medicines.
chunks.dispose: Do not mix it with wet or dry waste. Hand it over at a designated special care waste collection point.
chunks.source: SWM Rules, 2026 (MoEFCC)
